Table of best MAGs
```{r}
# Start with a clean slate
rm(list=ls())

library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)

winners <- read.csv("F:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/dRep_output/data_tables/Widb.csv", header = TRUE)

```

Make new folder that contains all of the winning bins as found in the dRep table that will feed into gtdbtk
```{r}

# Define input/output paths
bin_input_dir  <- "E:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/dRep_input"
gtdb_input_dir <- "E:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/gtdb_input"

# Create directory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(gtdb_input_dir)) {
  dir.create(gtdb_input_dir)
}

# Copy winner genomes
file.copy(
  from = file.path(bin_input_dir, winners$genome),
  to   = file.path(gtdb_input_dir, winners$genome),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

```
Run gtdbtk to identify down to genus - outside of R in an environment with gtdbtk already installed, I used mobaxterm where I have everything setup to run metabolic. This is the line I ran using the folder we just created above with winning bins.  

gtdbtk classify_wf \
  --genome_dir /data/millerl/Planktothrix_microbiomes/Planktothrix_microbiomes/gtdb_input \
  --out_dir /data/millerl/Planktothrix_microbiomes/Planktothrix_microbiomes/gtdb_output \
  --cpus 8 \
  --skip_ani_screen \
  --extension fa


Merge back into R
```{r}
gtdb <- read.delim("F:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/gtdb_output/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv", header = TRUE)

# Remove .fa extension from genome names for matching
winners <- winners %>%
  mutate(genome_base = sub("\\.fa$", "", genome))

# Merge using cleaned genome names
merged <- winners %>%
  left_join(gtdb, by = c("genome_base" = "user_genome"))

# Extract genus name from classification string
merged$genus <- sub(".*;g__([^;]+).*", "\\1", merged$classification)
#do it in this data frame as well, will be helpful to see all bins genus later
gtdb$genus <- sub(".*;g__([^;]+).*", "\\1", gtdb$classification)

```



still need contigs, can get it from dreps run of checkm (HEY HEY HEY for some reason, the checkm version run through drep showed far more # of contigs than when checkm is run on its own)
```{r}
#this file is messy so have to do a few things to it
# Step 1: Read TSV as plain text
checkm <- read_tsv("F:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/dRep_output/data/checkM/checkM_outdir/storage/bin_stats_ext.tsv", col_names = c("file", "metadata"), col_types = "cc")

# Step 2: Convert the Python dict-like strings to valid JSON
checkm <- checkm %>%
  mutate(
    metadata_json = str_replace_all(metadata, "'", '"'),   # replace single quotes with double quotes
    metadata_json = str_replace_all(metadata_json, "None", "null")  # handle Python None if present
  )

# Step 3: Parse JSON into a list-column
checkm <- checkm %>%
  mutate(metadata_parsed = map(metadata_json, ~fromJSON(.x, simplifyDataFrame = TRUE)))

# Step 4: Optionally, unnest into a flat table
checkm <- checkm %>%
  unnest_wider(metadata_parsed)

# Select only the desired columns
checkm <- checkm[, c("file", "# contigs")]

```


Now keep all columns from full_filtered but only keep Bin.Id that are in winners
```{r}

final_data <- semi_join(checkm, winners, by = c("file" = "genome"))

#no longer using marker lineage for taxonomy as it didnt go down to genus, so use genus from merged instead
final_data <- final_data %>%
  left_join(merged %>% dplyr::select(genome, genus, contamination, completeness, size), 
  by = c("file" = "genome"))  %>% 
  mutate(file = sub("\\.fa$", "", file)) 

```

Rename and organize columns
```{r}
final_data <- final_data %>%
  rename(
    `Bin Identity` = `genus`,
    `Culture Origin` = `file`,
    `Bin completeness` = `completeness`,
    `Bin contamination` = `contamination`,
    `Number of contigs` = `# contigs`,
    `Size of genome (bp)` = `size`
  )

#order it
final_data <- final_data %>%
  dplyr::select(
    `Bin Identity`, 
    `Culture Origin`, 
    `Bin completeness`, 
    `Bin contamination`, 
    `Number of contigs`, 
    `Size of genome (bp)`
  ) %>%
  arrange(`Bin Identity`)

```



export
```{r}
write.csv(final_data, "Best_MAGs.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
